# E-ink Usability Checklist: PB Store on the Reader

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for paged lists, touch targets, screen refresh behavior, progress display without animation, plain three-part messages, offline browsing, the states of the app list and the restart wording are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md, constitution 2.1.0, the device-facts table in the spec's Background, and the message rules of feature 002 in `docs/installer-rules.md`). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]` and should be settled in the plan or by editing the spec. The look "of PB Notes feature 010 and PB Cloud" (FR-042) lives in the sibling projects and is not read here; items that depend on it are marked `[Dependency]`. Safety and recovery wording is in `install-safety.md`.

## Paged Lists and Navigation

- [x] CHK001 Is the number of apps per page, or the rule that fixes it, specified (for example by screen height and row height), and is the order of the list (by name, by catalog order, installed first) defined? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (160 px rows, about 9 per page, order by name then 'not in the catalog'), research R-13.
- [x] CHK002 Is it specified where the user lands after returning from a detail page, a plan, a message or a finished operation (the same page, the first page, the page of the app just changed)? [Gap, Spec §Story 1]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (back on the same page of the same list).
- [x] CHK003 Is the behavior of the page buttons defined at the first and last page and for a list that fits on one page (hidden, disabled, or "page 1 of 1"), so that a disabled control is not mistaken for a broken one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (disabled at the ends, hidden when it fits on one page), ui-pages.
- [x] CHK004 Are the interactions of search and paging defined (results are paged again, the page resets, the count of matches is shown), including the empty result ("no app matches") and an empty catalog? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-010, §Story 1 scenario 7]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-010 (paged from page 1, 'n of m apps', 'No app matches', empty catalog line).
- [x] CHK005 Is it stated when the search is applied (at each typed letter or on confirm), given that every letter on an e-ink screen with an on-screen keyboard costs a screen update? [Ambiguity, Spec §Story 1 scenario 7]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-010 (applied on the keyboard's confirm).
- [x] CHK006 Is "Hardware page keys MAY also turn the pages" decided (required, optional, or not for this feature), and is it stated what the page buttons do on the screen when the reader has such keys? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (hardware page keys are not used in this feature).

## Touch Targets and Legibility

- [x] CHK007 Is "a clear gap to the next one" quantified, and is it stated which controls the 10 mm rule covers (list rows, page buttons, top-bar icon controls, dialog buttons, the keys of the keyboard shown for the search)? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §SC-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (120 px, 16 px gap, which controls; the reader's own keyboard is outside the rule).
- [x] CHK008 Is the 10 mm figure justified or marked as an assumption, and is a way to measure it given that does not depend on a ruler on the real reader (a size in pixels derived from the screen's resolution and size)? [Assumption, Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §SC-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 and SC-009 (120 px at 300 ppi, checked by check-ui-style.sh and DS-10).
- [x] CHK009 Are minimum text size and contrast defined for the grey levels of the screen (list text, the one-line description, messages, the plan text), instead of only a size for controls? [Gap, Spec §FR-042]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (32 px, black on white, grey only for disabled controls; DS-10 may tighten), Clarifications.
- [x] CHK010 Are the top-bar icon controls required to carry a text label or a text description, since an icon alone may not say what Refresh, Search, Settings or About does? [Gap, Spec §FR-042]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (text label on every top-bar icon control).
- [x] CHK011 Is the feedback to a tap defined when nothing may animate (what shows that a tap was received, and how fast), and is it consistent with ignoring further taps while an operation runs? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-024]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (pressed state at once; disabled while an operation runs), FR-024.

## Screen Refresh and "No Animation"

- [x] CHK012 Does the spec define when a partial refresh is allowed and when a full refresh is required (page turn, return from a dialog, after a number of partial refreshes), since the request names partial and full refresh and the spec contains neither term? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-017]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (full refresh at start, page-kind change, every 10th page turn, on leaving; DS-10 tunes), ui-pages Refresh policy.
- [x] CHK013 Is "animation" defined well enough to be checked (spinners, blinking cursor, kinetic or continuous scroll, fade, a changing progress bar between figures), including whether the visible flash of a full refresh counts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-017, §FR-042]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (animation defined; the full-refresh flash is not animation), ui-pages.
- [x] CHK014 Is "no more often than about every two seconds" replaced by a number with a tolerance, and is it said whether a Cancel tap during a long step is answered at once, outside that limit? [Ambiguity, Measurability, Spec §FR-017]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (once every 2 seconds; Cancel answers at once).
- [x] CHK015 Is ghosting addressed (a remaining image of the previous screen after dialogs and long lists), for example by a rule for a full refresh at the start of an operation and at its end? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-009 (full refresh when the page kind changes, so at the start and end of an operation), research R-13.

## Progress Display

- [x] CHK016 Is the content of the progress figure defined for each step (download, verification, writing, repair, "Update all"), including what is shown when a step has no known total and what shows overall position such as "app 2 of 3"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017, §FR-021]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (count done and seconds elapsed when no total; 'app n of m'), ui-pages Progress.
- [x] CHK017 Is the state of the Cancel control after the commit point specified (hidden, disabled with a reason, or held until finish with a message), and is it consistent with "Cancel until the commit point" and the home-key rule? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §FR-025]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (Cancel hidden after the commit point with the line 'Finishing; this cannot be cancelled').
- [x] CHK018 Is it specified where and when the screen says that the store switched Wi-Fi on and off again, so that the notice is not lost between progress screens? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, §SC-012]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (line on the progress page while on; result page says it was switched off), ui-pages.
- [x] CHK019 Is a rule given for long steps with no visible change (for example verifying a large package), so the user can tell a working reader from a frozen one without animation? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-017]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (seconds elapsed redrawn every 2 s shows a working reader).

## Plain Three-Part Messages

- [x] CHK020 Is the rule "texts for conditions that also exist in the installer MUST be the installer's texts" consistent with texts that name the computer or the USB cable (for example the next step of `E-INS-26`, "check the clock of the computer"), which do not apply on the reader? [Conflict, Spec §FR-019; `docs/installer-rules.md`]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-019 and research R-14 (installer wording except the next step; store-rules table).
- [x] CHK021 Are the store-only conditions that get an `E-STO-nn` id listed (wrong clock, low battery, launcher fallback, and so on), or is the set left open while the success criteria promise a message for each? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-006]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/store-rules.md (E-STO-01..10, W-STO-01..03 listed).
- [x] CHK022 Is the maximum length of a message defined so that all three parts fit on one screen without paging, and is it said what is cut first when a rule id, a path and a next step do not fit? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-019 (600 characters, path shortened to 60, id and third part never cut), store-rules test.
- [x] CHK023 Are the buttons of an error message defined (close only, retry, open the log) and is it stated whether a message stays available after it was closed (log screen entry, last message)? [Gap, Spec §FR-019, §FR-039]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-019 (one OK button; message also in the log), ui-pages Result.
- [x] CHK024 Is the third part ("what to do") defined for each of the three reader states ("unchanged", "restored to the previous state", "repair needed") in terms of things the user can do on the reader itself, and is the wrong-clock message specified down to the format of the date it shows? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-019]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-019 (third part per reader state) and FR-005 (date as YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

## Offline Browsing

- [x] CHK025 Is "offline" defined: Wi-Fi off, Wi-Fi on without internet, or no refresh tapped? The spec says the store switches Wi-Fi on for a user action, so is it clear what the list shows and which buttons it offers before any action? [Ambiguity, Spec §Story 1 scenario 5, §FR-001, §FR-012]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-012 ('offline' needs no definition: the list never needs a connection; Refresh always offered).
- [x] CHK026 Is it specified whether Install, Update and Check are shown and enabled on the cached list, and whether tapping Install on an old cached entry first refreshes the catalog or uses the cached signed entry as it is? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-015]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-001 (Install, Update and Check first refresh the catalog, then download), engine ensure_catalog.
- [x] CHK027 Is "last updated <date>" consistent with a wrong reader clock (the date is the reader's own, which is exactly what may be wrong), and is the catalog's generation date shown anywhere the user browses? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-038, §Edge Cases "clock"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-012 (the date is the reader's clock and may be wrong; the catalog's own date is in Settings), research R-09.
- [x] CHK028 Are the three offline start states each given a screen: cached catalog valid, no catalog yet, cached catalog discarded because its signature check failed? Is the difference visible to the user? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, §FR-012, §Edge Cases]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-012 (never downloaded vs discarded with E-STO-09 are visibly different), ui-pages Home.

## States of the App List

- [x] CHK029 Is the list's own wording consistent: FR-008 and Story 1 say "exactly one of the four states", yet apps not in the catalog get a fifth label, "not in the catalog", and notes are added; is the difference between state, note and label defined? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, §Story 1 scenario 1]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-008 (states vs notes vs the fifth label, already defined) and ui-pages States table.
- [x] CHK030 Is each state shown by text and not only by position, grey tone or icon, since the screen has no colour? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-008 and ui-pages (words plus an icon, never colour or position alone), research R-13.
- [x] CHK031 Is there a table of the actions offered per state and per note (install, update, remove, check, none), and does it cover the store's own entry, a pending repair, and an installed version that was withdrawn? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013, §FR-023]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md States and actions table (store itself, repair pending, withdrawn).
- [x] CHK032 Is it stated where "update available" shows both versions (list row or detail page), and where the user sees that an update of the store is prepared and takes effect at the next opening? [Gap, Spec §Story 3 scenario 1, §FR-032]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md (both versions on the row/detail; staged self-update note), spec FR-032.
- [x] CHK033 Is the order in which several notes appear defined (for example "update available" together with "changed since install" and "from a local file"), and is the row's room for them bounded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md (order of the notes defined).

## Restart Wording and Device Facts

- [x] CHK034 Is the request to say "plainly whether the reader has to be restarted" reconciled with the rule to say that it "may" have to be restarted, and is it said why the plain form is not yet possible? [Conflict, Spec §FR-018, §Background device facts]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Background and FR-018 ('may' is the honest wording until DS-05; the wording table changes in one place).
- [x] CHK035 Does the spec define what each verified outcome changes in the wording (restart needed, not needed, entry shown without restart, behavior for a missing file), and in which texts, so that the change can be checked and not only "changed in one place"? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions "device facts", §SC-011]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md 'Result wording' and research R-11 (restart_wording table, a test per combination).
- [x] CHK036 Are the wording rules defined for every operation that changes what the reader shows: install, update, remove, adopt (a record only, so presumably nothing to restart), a repair that changed the desktop configuration, and the self-update (the next opening of PB Store, not a restart of the reader)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, §FR-032]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md Result wording by operation (install, update, remove, adopt, repair, self-update).
- [x] CHK037 Is the difference between "restart the reader" and "open PB Store again" kept clear in the texts, and are the steps to restart the reader (or a pointer to them) part of the requirement? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-032]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md (self-update text says 'open PB Store again', not a reader restart), spec FR-032.
- [x] CHK038 Is "noticeably longer" for the next start of the reader quantified from the observation, or is the observation's source cited (research §18 of feature 002), so the claim is not stronger than the evidence? [Clarity, Spec §Background, §FR-018]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Background (the observation is the owner's, from feature 002 research §18; not a measurement).

## Acceptance Criteria and Traceability

- [x] CHK039 Do the success criteria cover the e-ink requirements beyond SC-009 (paging position, refresh behavior, progress update rate, message length, readable text size, restart wording equal to the verified facts)? [Coverage, Spec §SC-001, §SC-005, §SC-009]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec SC-009 (px, text size), SC-001, SC-005; ui-pages walks and the refresh/progress rules are tested (tasks T011, T069).
- [x] CHK040 Is "the look follows PB Notes (feature 010) and PB Cloud" checkable from this repository (a short list of the elements that are required: top bar, rounded dialogs, paged lists), or does it depend on documents that are not here? [Dependency, Measurability, Spec §FR-042]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: contracts/ui-pages.md lists the required elements (top bar, rounded dialogs, paged lists, no animation, sizes).

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Most likely to change the spec: CHK012 (no refresh rules at all), CHK020 (installer texts name the computer), CHK029 (four states versus the fifth label), CHK034 and CHK035 (restart wording versus unverified facts), CHK025 and CHK026 (what "offline" and the cached Install mean).
